accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE English programmes of study (2013), English Appendix 2 Year 2 ('correct choice and consistent use of present tense and past tense throughout writing'; 'use of the progressive form of verbs in the present and past tense to mark actions in progress [for example, she is drumming, he was shouting]'; terminology verb, tense (past, present)), Appendix 1 Year 1-2 spelling rules for -ed (jumped; baked: add d after e; patted/hummed: double after a short vowel), Common Core L.1.1e, L.2.1d and L.4.1b, and the NC glossary note that English has no future tense form. The lab's 'Now' zone only uses progressive forms, so it never claims the simple present means 'right now'; the adult text explains habits versus in-progress use.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS1 errors: over-regularising irregular verbs (runned, goed, sitted in Odd ones, the run prediction, the ed challenge tag, m2), spelling the ending by sound (jumpt, hopt, the Add -ed prediction, sound tag), the doubling rule confused with another word (hoped vs hopped, dbl tag, m8), double e (bakeed, m1), helper agreement (the boys is / the birds is: 'The birds means more than one, so use are', one tag, p3), was + -ing read as now (was tag, the He was shouting prediction, m4), and tense drift in a story (Keep it the same, mix tag, m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtense is built on a Yesterday-to-Now timeline: sentence cards are dropped into the past or now zone, the progressive step plots a dot with a wavy 'still going on' bar at the time the helper verb names, and the story step lays out three lines with tappable verb tiles that flip to the corrected form. Shingle similarity is 5.9% with flag_poss.js, 5.4% with flag_agree.js and 5.0% with flag_nph.js, far under the 30% limit.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rules by trying: dropping 'I played.' on Now bounces with 'ends in -ed. It is done'; picking were for 'Sam ___ running' under a Now dot says 'going on now, so use is or are', and are says 'Sam means just one, so use is', so the two choices (time and number) are separated; the done line then states the rule. Probed in Chromium on an iPhone 13 viewport: drag to a zone, drag a tile to the slot and every button twin give the expected message.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the next task disproves: 'with a t: jumpt' (the jumpt tile then bounces with 'It sounds like t, but the past ending is spelled ed'), 'Now' for 'He was shouting' (the timeline puts was + -ing in the past), and 'runned' for the past of run (runned bounces in Odd ones). A.reveal quotes the child's own guess in the done line.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers; why() names each slip: mix ('The sentence says yesterday or last week, so the verb must be past too'), ed ('That verb is an odd one. It does not take -ed'), was ('Was + -ing means it was going on in the past, not now'), done, one ('The boys are more than one, so use are'), dbl and sound. Wrong moves inside the lab also name the slip, for example 'Bake has an e already. Do not write two.'

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK -0.3 against the family kid target of 5.0, in short concrete sentences ('Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped.'). Adult text measures FK 8.6 against 10.0 and uses the precise terms for the age band: verb, tense, past tense, present tense, progressive form, helper verb, -ing participle, regular and irregular verbs, subject agreement, with the Year 2 and Common Core references.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed; the explanation's largest 6-word-shingle overlap with any other lesson is 0.3% (Commas in lists, Expanded noun phrases). Kid paragraphs cover tense, -ed, odd verbs, the progressive and consistency; adult paragraphs give curriculum placement, the grammar of be + -ing and the no-future-tense note, the three spelling rules, four named mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for all six steps: the two timeline zones with calendar and clock pictures fit side by side; the four helper tiles is, are, was, were fit one row; the story lines scale down to fit 390 px with verb tiles still large; young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall and wrap without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five Show me tasks completed, the challenge appeared, axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme and there were no console or page errors. Every drag has a button twin (Yesterday/Now, every word tile, every story verb), and the canvas aria-label is updated with every prompt and message.

sources: DfE (2013) English programmes of study: key stages 1 and 2, English Appendix 1 (spelling) and Appendix 2 (vocabulary, grammar and punctuation), Year 1 and Year 2; glossary entries for tense, progressive and future
Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Language L.1.1e, L.2.1d, L.4.1b
Cambridge Dictionary, Grammar: Present continuous (I am working) and Past simple (I worked)
